key_insight: Hyperball wraps a base optimizer to keep weight and update Frobenius norms fixed, improving pretraining speed and scaling behavior beyond standard decoupled weight decay.
engineering_relevance: For large language model pretraining, Hyperball can yield better token-efficiency and more transferable hyperparameters across model widths and depths.
method: Add Hyperball on top of an optimizer such as Adam or Muon.
Constrain each weight matrix and its optimizer update to fixed Frobenius norms.
Use this norm control instead of relying on constant decoupled weight decay.
evidence_signal: On Qwen3-style models up to 1.2B parameters, Muon Hyperball achieved about 20–30% token-equivalent speedup over weight-decay baselines and improved learning-rate transfer.
watch_item: The method depends on careful norm-setting for each matrix, so implementation details and compatibility with existing optimizer pipelines may affect results.
paper_title: Fantastic Pretraining Optimizers and Where to Find Them II: Hyperball Optimization
